question: ‘Mintonette’ is related to which of the following sports?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Volleyball**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mintonette** was the original name for the sport now known as Volleyball.
 
• It was invented in 1895 by **William G. Morgan**, a physical education director in Holyoke, Massachusetts.
 
• Morgan initially created the game as a **less intense alternative to basketball** for older businessmen.
 
• The game was renamed to Volleyball in 1896 during a demonstration at the International YMCA Training School in Springfield, Massachusetts, to better describe the objective of the game - volleying the ball back and forth over a net.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **William G. Morgan**

 
 
• He was a graduate of the International YMCA Training School, where he met James Naismith, the inventor of basketball.
 
• Morgan sought to blend elements of basketball, baseball, tennis, and handball to create Mintonette.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Volleyball**
 
 
• The original rules allowed for an unlimited number of players and nine innings, with each team allowed three outs per inning.
 
• By 1916, the sport had evolved to include the modern concept of rotation and set and spike techniques.
 
• Volleyball became an Olympic sport in 1964 during the Tokyo Summer Olympics.
 
 
 
• **International Growth**
 
 
• The Fédération Internationale de Volleyball (FIVB) was founded in 1947 to govern the sport worldwide.
 
• Volleyball is now played by over 800 million people globally, with significant popularity in Brazil, Russia, Japan, and many European countries.
